questions.stem: A planner asks for project K to be in the plan, in whichever of its start years 2028, 2029 or 2030 the optimizer prefers. How is the override written on the start variables x(K, t)?

options.text: Lower bound 1 on each of K's three start variables
options.says: That forces K to start in all three years, which its once row forbids: the model becomes infeasible.

options.text: One row: K's three start variables sum to exactly 1
options.says: Right: "in some year" is a rule on a sum, so it needs a row, like override_P024.

options.text: Upper bound 1 on each of K's three start variables
options.says: Every binary start variable already has upper bound 1, so nothing changes and K may still be left out.

options.text: Lower bound 1 on K's start variable for 2028 alone
options.says: That fixes the year to 2028, taking the choice of year away from the optimizer.

origin.section: An Override on Start Variables Is a Bound, Not a Row

questions.stem: Variable x(K, 2030) had upper bound 0, set by an earlier override. A second override, "K in 2029", then set it to 0 again. The planner withdraws the second override only. What does the undo set the upper bound of x(K, 2030) to?

options.text: 1, since undoing the second override resets the binary to bounds 0 and 1
options.says: That undoes the first override too; an undo restores what the bound was before the override it reverses.

options.text: 1, since withdrawing the second override frees every variable it touched
options.says: The second override found the bound already at 0; freeing it would drop a decision no one withdrew.

options.text: 0, since a bound the second override set can never change again
options.says: Bounds can be set again at any time; that is how undo works. The answer is 0 for another reason.

options.text: 0, the value it held before the second override was applied
options.says: Right: apply records each variable's old bounds, and undo puts exactly those back.

origin.section: An Override Is Data, and Restoring the Bounds Undoes It

questions.stem: An override says "start P in 2031", but P may start only in 2027, 2028 or 2029. The override code sets the upper bound of every start variable of P for a year other than 2031 to 0. What does the solve return?

options.text: INFEASIBLE, since P has no start variable for 2031
options.says: Nothing forces P in: its variables are all 0, which every row accepts.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with a plan in which P is not funded
options.says: Right: every existing year is closed, so the request for P turns into dropping P, as with P038.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with P started in 2029, the nearest year
options.says: 2029's variable has upper bound 0 like the others; the model has no notion of a nearest year.

options.text: OPTIMAL, with P started in 2031 as the planner asked
options.says: There is no variable for 2031, so no plan can start P then.

origin.section: A Conflicting Override Makes the Model Infeasible, or Quietly Changes It
